newsitem.title: USA: RP Rorer submits Lovenox NDA for thrombosis.
newsitem.headline: RP Rorer submits Lovenox NDA for thrombosis.

text.p: Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc Thursday said it submitted a supplemental New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for Lovenox injection to treat deep-vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism.

Deep-vein thrombosis, the formation of blood clots in the deep veins, can sometimes lead to pulmonary embolism. Pulmonary embolism occurs when a clot circulates and lodges in the lung, potentially leading to sudden death.
Venous thromboembolic disease (deep-vein thrombosis and/or pulmonary embolism) is responsible for more than 400,000 hospitalizations and up to 200,000 deaths each year in the U.S.
Lovenox is the only low-molecular-weight heparin cleared for marketing in the U.S. for the prevention of deep-vein thrombosis in both hip-replacement and knee-replacement surgery.

The NDA was based in part on the results of two pivotal multicenter, randomized clinical trials that compared Lovenox with standard heparin, the drug most commonly used to treat deep-vein thrombosis. An analysis of data from both studies showed that Lovenox was equivalent to adjusted-dose continuous-infusion heparin therapy in preventing recurrent venous thromboembolic disease in patients with acute deep-vein thrombosis, with or without pulmonary embolism. The safety profile of both Lovenox once daily and Lovenox twice daily was comparable to that of continuous-infusion heparin therapy.
Lovenox, which is the number-one selling low-molecular-weight heparin in the world, was cleared for marketing in the United States and Canada in 1993.
